question: A to D are sitting in a row not necessarily in the same order. Two of them are facing in one direction and the other two are facing in the opposite direction. B and D are the extremes and face the North. A is facing the same direction as his neighbour on his left. D is to the left of A. What is the order of seating from left to right?
solution:
**Given: **A to D are sitting in a row. Two of them are facing in one direction and the other two are facing in the opposite direction.

1) B and D are the extremes and face the North.

As B and D both faces north and it is given that equal number of people faces north and south, therefore the rest will be facing south.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a810c4618343e8c7162aac103672c75f94b6aca88c1937fd8e2f643a32514a8c.png] 

2) D is to the left of A.

3) A is facing the same direction as his neighbour on his left.

After positioning A, only one position is left which will be occupied by the only left i.e. C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81a98919249bfbc4194ea222d97cb62d8a49b7122f31bec6582fe8e5cdd59e26.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement 'BACD' is the order of seating from left to right.

Hence, **"Option 4"** is the correct answer.
